q: The United States officially announces the resumption of large-scale airstrikes on mainland Iran
basis: The case for: Trump's September 23 threat to annihilate Iran and reports of plans to resume bombing after the midterms. The case against: oil prices hovering around $100 a barrel and the room for negotiation after the election. Reports on October 27 and 28 said Washington had told allies to prepare for a post-midterm operation and for Iranian retaliation. On October 31, reports said Washington had told Gulf allies that a short, intense strike could come as early as November 4, and on the night of November 2 U.S. forces carried out a limited strike on an air-defense site around Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz. On November 9, after meeting Qatar's prime minister, President Trump said Iran was militarily effectively over and that the naval blockade would remain in place, and on Truth Social he said renewed strikes were quite unlikely. On November 10, after a G7 foreign ministers' meeting, Secretary of State Marco Rubio said military strikes were not needed if economic pressure was achieving the same objective. The short strike reported as possible around November 4 amounted to limited strikes around Qeshm Island, and Iran denies any talks and keeps the Strait of Hormuz closed.
rs: An official announcement by the White House or the U.S. Department of Defense
